conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code and passed the catalogue entry's agent brief (solve/487 page) to the model. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Opened Founders Online 02-01-02-0163 and 0361 in the browser: abstracts only, 'partly in code; key not found', printed in King, Life and Correspondence 3:436-38, 472-73. The 25 Apr despatch is no. 14, not no. 15.
Grepped the archive.org text of Life and Correspondence vol. 3: both despatches printed in full; the 25 Apr final paragraph carries the footnote 'Italics in cipher'.

Viewed the page images pp. 438, 472-473 and transcribed the italics: 25 Apr, 96 of 124 words of the final paragraph in 13 runs (George III's relapse); 8 June, only 'Lord Hawkesbury and Mr. Addington'.
Looked for images of NARA M30 roll 9 online to transcribe the code groups and rebuild the code from the printed crib: none found.

outcome.method_basis: Both despatches are printed in full in King, Life and Correspondence 3 (1896) 436-38 and 472-73, with the coded words set in italics ('Italics in cipher').
outcome.notes: Printed in 1896 with the coded words marked; the coded duplicates (NARA M30 roll 9) were not seen and the code was not identified. Catalogue entry 487 removed, no write-up.

texts.label: 25 Apr 1801, no. 14
texts.summary: King reports the Baltic campaign, Copenhagen, Russia, Hanover and Egypt in clear; the coded final paragraph says George III has relapsed after returning to business too early and may never completely recover, which adds to the ministers' difficulties.
texts.note: Decryption: King, Life and Correspondence 3 (1896) p. 438, coded words in italics (underscored in the file). No transcription of the code groups: microfilm not online.

reading_review.note: The decryption is the 1896 printed text, ordinary English prose; the low shape score comes from the italics markers (underscores) and the line breaks of the page transcription, not from holes. Every sentence reads.

texts.label: 8 June 1801, no. 21
texts.summary: King reports the King's recovery, Egypt, the Baltic settlement and French invasion preparations; the coded words name Lord Hawkesbury and Mr. Addington as the ministers who offered the United States by treaty any limitation of the right of search Britain conceded to another nation.
texts.note: Decryption: King, Life and Correspondence 3 (1896) p. 473, coded words in italics. No transcription of the code groups: microfilm not online.
